request.spec:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Only DRAFT claims can be edited now, and a voided claim keeps its number. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the acceptance spec.

**Server**
- `ClaimService.update` turns down an edit of any claim that isn't a DRAFT. It uses a new `ClaimNotEditableException` (HTTP 409), so a refused edit saves nothing and writes nothing to the audit file.
- `changeStatus` no longer clears the number when a claim is voided. A voided claim that had been opened keeps its number, and `CLAIM_VOIDED` ends with `number=N`. A DRAFT that is voided never had a number, so its record has none, which is what the spec expects. Numbers are still never reused.
- No schema change was needed, since the number column already exists.

**Front end** (`claims.ts`)
- Pressing Edit on a claim that isn't a DRAFT doesn't open the editor. It shows the error on the claim (`claim-error`), telling the user to void it and add a new one.
- If the page is out of date (say another user opened the claim meanwhile), the server refuses the save and the form error now says only a DRAFT claim can be edited.

**Worth knowing:**
- Claims voided before this change already had their number cleared, so they will still show no number.
- I left the comment in the old migration `V8__claim_number.sql` as it was, even though it still says voiding clears the number. Editing a migration that has already run would break the database's record of applied migrations.
- SETTLED claims can no longer be edited either, since the request allows edits only on a DRAFT.
